public_rationale: The historical reading is supported. Separate evaluations document problems with changing entity states, implicit workplace assumptions, and physical predictions beyond familiar video examples. These are repeated shortcomings across the approaches discussed. The video study also reports strong successes in familiar settings, so the evidence supports unreliability across situations, not an absence of learned capabilities or a proof that scaling can never work.
limitations: Reliable commonsense remains an interpretive standard.
The video experiments use simplified physical environments rather than every commercial video model.
The studies are samples of capabilities, not an exhaustive evaluation of all AI.
The January 2024 item dates the reported evaluation version; individual test execution dates are not specified.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The hope that reliable commonsense will emerge from large text and video datasets has repeatedly proven unrealistic.

statement.excerpt: Hoping that reliable commonsense will simply “emerge” from large databases and video has proven unrealistic, again and again.
statement.document_title: AI still lacks “common” sense, 70 years later

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that large-scale text and video learning had repeatedly fallen short of dependable commonsense across varied situations by publication.
The claim does not deny useful learned knowledge or success on particular tasks, and it does not establish permanent impossibility.
Repeated evidence must cover multiple evaluations and both language-based and video-based approaches.
The retrospective period runs from 2020, when the surrounding discussion introduces GPT-3, through January 5, 2025.
criteria.support_condition: Multiple evaluations within the period document recurring commonsense failures in language-based systems and failures of physical generalization in video-based systems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations establish broad, repeatable commonsense reliability in both model classes, making the claimed pattern of shortcomings inaccurate.

evidence.explanation: The reported evaluation concerns entity and attribute changes in procedural text, a concrete component of everyday reasoning. It establishes a shortcoming in that task family rather than a universal absence of commonsense.

evidence.locator: Section 7.3, Common Agent Failures, Lack of commonsense
evidence.explanation: The study identifies commonsense-related failures in a multi-model workplace-agent evaluation. Its overall task failures have several causes, so they cannot all be counted as commonsense failures.

Controlled video experiments found that scaling did not deliver dependable physical predictions outside the training distribution. The same results show substantial successes within familiar distributions and some improvements on new combinations.
